absent: Full field layouts of MSI descriptors, IRQ domains, IRQ data and chips, device MSI storage, control ranges, affinity descriptors, and firmware specifiers.
Numeric values of bus tokens, MSI flags, virtual IRQ flags, trigger types and masks, domain flags, and error statuses.
MSI domain creation, vector allocation, activation and deactivation internals, and sysfs group and attribute population details.
Firmware specifier conversion, OF node handling, revmap sizing and creation, and linear versus tree threshold policy.
Lock ordering and interrupt context rules across MSI mutex, domain root mutex, descriptor locks, and RCU protection.
Kexec EOI versus shutdown ordering guarantees and VM-forward clearing semantics.
Affinity validation, managed lifecycle, reservation mode interaction, and forced threading effects.
Debug directory creation, lifetime, and per-operation debug hook contracts.

findings.text: MSI sysfs helpers exist in two build variants, one managing per-vector attribute lifetime and one accepting the same interface as a no-op success path.
Reservation mode eligibility is confined to PCI MSI family transports, requires reactivation support without a no-mask restriction, and depends on a mask-capable descriptor.
PCI MSI allocation failure handling distinguishes unsupported transports from retryable multi-vector shortfalls and from partial success, signalling retry separately from terminal shortage.

Virtual IRQ initialization separates reservation clearing, managed shutdown when no online CPU can serve a managed interrupt, and activation with reservation state adjusted for later final assignment.
MSI allocation information prefers a domain-provided template when present and otherwise delegates preparation to the domain operations.
MSI domain teardown validates a caller-supplied range, resolves the targeted domain, invokes a custom free hook when available, and optionally releases descriptors.
Device MSI control ranges are valid only within the configured domain count and hardware size with ordered bounds.
Descriptor store reclamation requires the device MSI mutex and skips descriptors that remain associated rather than freeing them.
Generic MSI IRQ release covers only associated entries, ensures deactivation before release, detaches optional sysfs state, and clears the recorded IRQ number.
Device-tree IRQ creation converts an OF specifier into a firmware specifier and resolves it through the generic firmware mapping path.
Mapping disposal is a no-op for empty or unknown virtual IRQs and otherwise follows either a hierarchical single-IRQ release or a disassociate plus descriptor release path.
Single-IRQ hierarchical release has a dispatching variant that separates wired MSI device handling from generic release and an empty variant for builds without hierarchy.
Wired-to-MSI release validates device association and default-domain ownership under descriptor guard before releasing the single descriptor index.
Range-based MSI free accepts domain identity and bounds and forwards them through the locked teardown path.
Hardware to virtual IRQ resolution uses read-side protection for reverse-map lookup, with a separate direct validation path for no-map domains and a global default fallback.
Single-cell translation accepts one or two cells, takes hardware identity from the first cell, and treats a missing trigger cell as no trigger type.
Two- and three-cell translation selects hardware identity by cell count and derives masked trigger type from the trailing cell, rejecting other counts.
A shared simple domain operations table binds generic translation to the one-or-two-cell interpretation.
Hierarchy disconnection marks the per-IRQ chip reference as not connected while leaving the mapping otherwise intact.
Hierarchical IRQ release resets per-IRQ state level by level toward the parent, with the top-level variant additionally clearing handler state.
Reverse-map repair requires the domain root mutex and updates either the linear slot or the tree slot for mapped domains.
Hierarchy push preserves existing per-IRQ state for rollback, commits a new level only on successful allocation, and refuses busy or mismatched configurations.
Hierarchy pop only applies at the current top level with saved parent state present, then releases the level and restores the preserved state with reverse-map repair.
Hierarchy push and pop serialize mapping mutation under the domain root mutex and perform allocation outside a race-free action check.
Parent IRQ allocation reports unavailability without a parent and otherwise delegates to the parent hierarchy.
IRQ domain debug state comprises a hierarchy root entry plus a flag-name table and recursive parent display of identity, size, usage and flags.
Kexec shutdown walks all IRQ descriptors, acknowledges in-progress interrupts where supported, and shuts down started lines.
This IRQ management unit uses a fixed log prefix, a boot-enabled force-threading switch, a global default affinity mask, and a per-CPU scratch mask.
Hard-IRQ synchronization tolerates missing descriptors and reports whether threaded activity remains.
Affinity query and forced affinity operations delegate to internal descriptor-based helpers.
Affinity descriptor updates require a stopped unmanaged interrupt, temporarily drop activation across the update, and record managed state and mask before restoring activation.
Affinity hint updates record the hint under descriptor protection and optionally trigger an affinity change.
Reclamation intentionally leaks a descriptor that is still associated, signalling a reference lifetime violation rather than freeing in use.
Push and pop reject descriptors with active handlers as busy, since concurrent handling cannot be made safe across hierarchy mutation.
A neutral trigger type and a sense mask define how firmware-provided trigger bits are normalized.
Distinct negative statuses signal invalid parameters, busy state, shortage, unsupported operation, missing connection, and allocation failure across mapping and hierarchy paths.
